office_does: The Clark County Council adopts the county budget and property-tax levies, sets councilmanic taxes and fees, adopts the growth-management comprehensive plan and land-use rules for unincorporated areas, and decides which county propositions go to voters.
race_blurb: First-term incumbent Glen Yung, who voted for the 2026 property-tax levy increase and a 0.1% housing sales tax, faces business owner Bryan Shull, who runs on a "tax-last" approach, lower fees and faster permitting, and treatment and accountability in place of housing-first strategies.

candidates.summary: First-term District 1 councilor and former banker and remodeling-business owner who runs on homelessness, housing affordability and public-safety investments.
highlights: Voted for the 1% general-fund levy increase in the 2026 county budget [S5]
Voted for the 0.1% sales tax for affordable housing and behavioral health: "we are experiencing a housing crisis" [S6]
Secured funding for a 120-bed shelter with integrated addiction and mental-health treatment [S1]
Backs "a balanced approach that addresses both crime and the root causes behind it" [S4]
Voted with the full council to put the Proposition 12 jail bond and Proposition 13 levy lid lift on the ballot [S8]

taxes.basis: Voted for the 2026 1% levy increases with banked capacity and for the 0.1% councilmanic housing sales tax, citing rising service costs and the housing crisis.

spending.basis: Pushes investment in shelter, treatment and housing now, while also citing a county-manager performance review and responsible budgeting.

housing.basis: Pairs public funding (housing sales tax) and mobile-home-park protections with supply measures (middle housing, faster permitting).

safety.basis: Explicitly balances law-enforcement investment and body cameras with treatment-linked shelter and root-cause approaches.

experience.basis: First-term incumbent running on his council record.

candidates.summary: Vancouver brewery and small-business owner and renewable-energy engineer, president of the Uptown Village Association, running for office for the first time.
highlights: Supports a "tax-last" approach: responsible budgeting before asking taxpayers to pay more [S1]
"We must address out of control spending" [S2]
Would cut permit fees and wait times and address fees and land-use rules that raise housing costs [S2]
Would replace housing-first and harm-reduction strategies with more treatment and accountability [S2]

taxes.basis: Repeatedly calls tax increases a burden and taxes a last resort after budget reprioritization, without pledging no new taxes.

spending.basis: Calls for addressing "out of control spending" and reprioritizing funds to core services before new revenue.

housing.basis: Housing plan centers on lower fees, streamlined permitting and land-use changes.

safety.basis: Supports law enforcement and wants treatment and accountability in place of housing-first and harm reduction.

climate.basis: Renewable-energy engineer who backs clean energy but frames it around affordability and reliability.

experience.basis: Political newcomer with business and nonprofit leadership but no public office.
